outline: 1133 Area of a Triangle using Trigonometry

examples.solution_text: Sides $p$ and $q$ touch the $120^{\circ}$ vertex. Side $r$ joins the other two vertices, so the opposite side is $r$.
The $6\text{ cm}$ side joins $P$ and $Q$. It does not reach vertex $R$, so the opposite angle is $R$.

(a) Side $f$ is opposite angle $F$: the side uses the matching lowercase letter.

(b) Angle $D$ is opposite side $d$: the angle uses the matching uppercase letter.

methods.description: Identify the side joining the two vertices other than the angle's vertex; it does not touch that vertex. Lettered, numerical and obtuse angles use the same method.

examples.derivation: The rays from L towards R and T form 120 degrees: atan2(2.07846, -1.2) is approximately 120 degrees. Sides p and q meet at L; side r joins R and T and does not touch L. Therefore r is opposite the marked angle. This follows the supplied booklet's opposite-side identification method.

The 6 cm label is placed beside segment PQ. Its endpoints are P and Q, leaving R as the only vertex it does not reach. Therefore angle R is opposite the measured side. The adapted measurement and orientation preserve the source exercise's method; diagram coordinates need not represent centimetres to scale.

Under the supplied convention, an opposite side and angle share a letter with lowercase for the side and uppercase for the angle. Thus angle F is opposite side f, and side d is opposite angle D. No diagram is necessary for this notation task.
